title: Affine principal chart and finite translate cover of a smooth generically affine trait group
statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with algebraically closed residue field $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], fraction field $K$, and a generator $\pi$ of its maximal ideal. Let $G$ be a smooth, separated group scheme of finite type over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]; its multiplication, identity and inverse satisfy the group diagrams. Assume $G_K=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-scheme]. Put $A=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ and, for $h\in A$, put $G_h=\{x\in G:h_x\in\mathcal O_{G,x}^{\times}\}$ with its open subscheme structure. There exist $f\in A$, an integer $n\geq1$, and sections $g_1,\ldots,g_n\in G(R)$ such that $G_f$ is affine and $G_f\cap G_k\ne\varnothing$, and such that, on putting $f_0=\pi\cdot1_A$ and $f_j=(L_{g_j}^{-1})^*f$ for $1\leq j\leq n$, one has $G=\bigcup_{j=0}^nG_{f_j}$ and every $G_{f_j}$ is affine. Here $L_g$ is left multiplication by the section $g$, $G_k=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $G(R)$ denotes the sections of $G\to S$. In particular $G_{f_0}=G_K$ and $G_{f_j}=L_{g_j}(G_f)$ for $j\geq1$. No connectedness hypothesis on either fibre is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/qrg.pdf: Proposition 3.1, printed p.5, the affine principal chart and its translates, citing Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models, p.161 Lemma 6. Finite subcover extracted using finite type; use algebraically closed residue field so closed points of the special fibre are rational. The seed is a global principal open, not just an arbitrary affine neighbourhood.

proof.text: The DVR $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal]. Its spectrum is Noetherian: the single affine chart has Noetherian coordinate ring and is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Hence $G$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is separated as a scheme by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated], and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. For any affine chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $G$, restriction is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], so $R\to B$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] and flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. In particular multiplication by $\pi$ is injective on $B$ by [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain]. It is therefore injective on the structure sheaf and on its global sections.

source.place: Tags 00PD, 01T6, 01V6, 00TA; scheme finiteness and flatness preparation.

proof.text: Both fibres are of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to their field bases makes them Noetherian. Smoothness of the fibres follows on the preceding affine charts from [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and to the special fibre over $k$: $G$ and $G_k$ are reduced, every generic point of $G$ lies in $G_K$, and $G_K$ is dense in every component of $G$. Both fibres are nonempty because the identity section has a point in each.

source.place: Tags 01T6, 00T4, 034E, 00HS; smooth fibre and generic-density preparation.

proof.text: There are finitely many generic points of $G$ and $G_k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. At a generic point of $G$ the local dimension is zero, since primes of a stalk correspond to generalizations and there is no strict generalization of a component's generic point. At a generic point $z$ of $G_k$, choose a Noetherian affine chart from the locally Noetherian cover of $G$. Its ring $B$ is flat over $R$ by step 1. The local fibre ring at $z$ has dimension zero, since its corresponding prime is minimal. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] gives $\dim\mathcal O_{G,z}=1+0=1$. All the stalks concerned are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Apply [lem-trf-codimension-one-points-affine-neighbourhood] to these finitely many points in the separated Noetherian scheme $G$: every quasi-compact open has finitely many components, by the Noetherian property and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. We obtain an affine open $U$ containing all of them. In particular $U$ is dense in $G$ and $U_k$ is dense in $G_k$.

source.place: Tags 00ON and 09NN; common affine neighbourhood of the generic points of both fibres.

proof.text: Put $E=G\setminus U$. Its finitely many irreducible components exist by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. By [lem-sfb-affine-open-boundary-codimension-one], the generic point $\xi$ of any such component has local dimension one in $G$. If $\xi$ lay in $G_k$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] in a Noetherian affine chart at $\xi$: $1=1+\dim\mathcal O_{G_k,\xi}$, hence the fibre local dimension is zero. Its prime is therefore minimal, so $\xi$ is a generic point of $G_k$, contrary to the choice of $U$. Every generic point of $E$ consequently lies in $G_K$. Each component is the closure of that point, so $E=\overline{E\cap G_K}$ in $G$.

source.place: Tag 0BCV and Tag 00ON; the affine boundary has no vertical component.

proof.text: Write $G_K=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and let $J\subset C$ define its closed subset $E_K$. For every minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of $C$, its point belongs to $U_K$, so $J\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$. There are finitely many such primes by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components], and at least one since the generic fibre contains the identity. Prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] supplies $a_K\in J$ outside all of them. Consequently $D(a_K)\subseteq U_K$, and $a_K$ is nonzero in the residue field at every generic point of $G_K$. By [lem-sfb-qcqs-functions-local-comparison], applied to $G\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with powers of $\pi$, $C=A[1/\pi]$. Write $a_K=h/\pi^d$ with $h\in A$ and $d\geq0$. Then $D(h|_{G_K})=D(a_K)$.

source.place: Tag 00DS and Tag 02KH (degree zero); choose a principal open dense in every generic component.

proof.text: Choose a point $x\in G_k$, for example the identity. The germ $h_x$ is nonzero. Indeed choose an irreducible component of $G$ containing $x$; its generic point $\eta$ lies in $G_K$ by step 2, and $h$ has nonzero residue there by step 5. If $h_x=0$, $h$ would vanish on a neighbourhood of $x$; every such neighbourhood contains $\eta$, a contradiction. The stalk $B=\mathcal O_{G,x}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and $\pi B$ lies in its maximal ideal. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with $M=B$ gives $\bigcap_m\pi^mB=0$. Thus $h$ cannot belong to $\pi^mA$ for arbitrarily large $m$. Let $N$ be the largest integer with $h\in\pi^NA$, and write $h=\pi^Nf$. Then $f\notin\pi A$ and $D(f|_{G_K})=D(a_K)$, since $\pi$ is invertible on the generic fibre.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (2); bound uniformizer divisibility at a nonzero special stalk.

proof.text: The kernel of $A\to\Gamma(G_k,\mathcal O_{G_k})$ is exactly $\pi A$. To see this without assuming surjectivity on global sections, let a global section restrict to zero on $G_k$. On every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\pi B)$, so the section is $\pi$ times a section of $B$. The quotients agree on overlaps because multiplication by $\pi$ is injective as a sheaf by step 1. They glue to a global quotient. The reverse containment is immediate. Hence $\bar f\ne0$. The fibre is reduced by step 2 and quasi-compact by step 2's Noetherian conclusion. If $f$ were a nonunit at every point of $G_k$, [lem-weil-pbc-qc-scheme-vanishing-section-nilpotent] would make $\bar f$ nilpotent; reducedness would make it zero. Thus $G_f\cap G_k$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 03GY, proof, vanishing section is nilpotent; local division and unique sheaf gluing written out.

proof.text: On $E_K$, $f$ has zero residue by steps 5--6, so $E_K\subseteq G\setminus G_f$. The latter is closed: on an affine chart it is the usual zero set of the restricted function. Step 4 therefore gives $E\subseteq G\setminus G_f$, and hence $G_f\subseteq U$. Thus $G_f=U_{f|_U}$ as open subschemes. Since $U$ is affine, [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies this open with the spectrum of the localization of $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ at $f|_U$. This proves its affineness.

source.place: Tag 01I3 (principal localization); conclude the seed principal open is affine.

proof.text: The nonempty open $W=G_f\cap G_k$ contains a closed point of $G_k$ by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], applied with closed subset $Z=G_k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], its residue field is $k$, giving $u\in W(k)$. Every closed point $y$ of $G_k$ is likewise a $k$-point. Form $v=y u^{-1}\in G_k(k)$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $V$ of $v$ in $G$. Its coordinate algebra is smooth over $R$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. The point $v$ is an $R$-algebra map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)\to k$. The pair $(R,\pi R)$ is henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Applying [lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting] with its $A=R$ and $I=\pi R$ lifts $v$ to a section $g\in V(R)\subseteq G(R)$. Its specialization is exactly $y u^{-1}$, so $y=L_g(u)\in L_g(G_f)$.

source.place: Tag 0478, Tag 00FV, Tag 0H74; rational special-fibre translations lift to R-sections.

proof.text: For any section $g$, the group diagrams give $L_{g^{-1}}\circ L_g=1=L_g\circ L_{g^{-1}}$, so $L_g$ is an automorphism. It carries the affine open $G_f$ to an affine open. The union $O=\bigcup_{g\in G(R)}L_g(G_f)$ is open and contains every closed point of $G_k$ by step 9. If the closed subset $G_k\setminus O$ were nonempty, [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] would supply a closed point of $G_k$ in it, a contradiction. Therefore $O$ contains all of $G_k$. Together with $G_K$, these opens cover $G$. Quasi-compactness of $G$ from step 1 gives finitely many sections $g_1,\ldots,g_n$ whose translates, together with $G_K$, cover $G$. Adjoin the identity section if necessary to ensure $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 0478 and elementary group identities/finite subcover; no connectedness used.

proof.text: Set $f_0=\pi\cdot1_A$ and $f_j=(L_{g_j}^{-1})^*f$. For an isomorphism the local-ring maps preserve and reflect units. Thus $x\in G_{f_j}$ if and only if $L_{g_j}^{-1}(x)\in G_f$, proving $G_{f_j}=L_{g_j}(G_f)$ as open subschemes. Also $R[1/\pi]=K$: every nonzero element of a DVR is a unit times a power of its uniformizer. On each affine chart, [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] identifies the open where $\pi$ is invertible with its base change to $R[1/\pi]$. These identifications glue, giving $G_{f_0}=G_K$. This open is affine by hypothesis, and each of the other opens is isomorphic to the affine $G_f$. Step 10 now gives all assertions, including the finite cover.

source.place: DVR uniformizer description (Tag 00PD), principal localization, and the definition of pullback; final identities.
